lines.trans: Folks, I was the most-voted city councilor in the city of Sao Paulo.
I am going to kill you guys!
Calm down, don't quit, otherwise it is going to look bad.
You have to get stripped of office.
How do we do that?
Say something really racist, like, Indigenous people are all cannibals.
Is it going to work?
Trust me.
Trust me.

meanings.note: Alone as vocative gente! it means folks/guys; with article a gente it means we/us with third-person singular verbs.

examples.text: Você acha que é melhor que a gente?
examples.trans: Do you think you're better than us?
Oh, folks, the meeting ran late.

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.
Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Member of a Brazilian municipal legislature (Câmara Municipal).

examples.text: Fui a vereadora mais votada da cidade.
examples.trans: I was the most-voted city councilor in the city.
She works as a city councilor.

meanings.note: Marks comparisons (mais que), negated continuation (não ... mais, not anymore), and the farewell até mais.
In the superlative a mais votada, designates the candidate who received the highest vote total.

examples.trans: I was the most-voted city councilor.

examples.text: Ele foi o deputado mais votado.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
A cidade de São Paulo refers to the municipality of São Paulo.

examples.text: Ela foi a mais votada da cidade.
examples.trans: She was the most voted in the city.

examples.text: São Paulo é uma cidade enorme.
examples.trans: São Paulo is a huge city.

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.
Eu vou matar vocês! is hyperbolic exasperation ('I'm going to kill you guys!').

examples.text: Eu vou matar vocês se isso der errado!
examples.trans: I am going to kill you guys if this goes wrong!

meanings.note: Plural addressee pronoun across Brazil, taking third-person plural verb forms.

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you all look closely, there are numbers.
Are you all going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Used standalone or as calma aí! to tell someone to slow down and relax.
A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.

desistir.gloss: to give up; drop out; quit

meanings.en: to give up; drop out; quit
meanings.note: Takes de before what one quits: desistir de ser candidata (to drop out of being a candidate).

examples.trans: I gave up on being a candidate.

meanings.note: One word when meaning 'otherwise' (as opposed to se não = 'if not').

examples.text: Não desiste, senão vai pegar mal.
examples.trans: Don't quit, otherwise it will look bad.
Run, or else we will be late.

meanings.note: Used for taking transport, grabbing items, or taking an apartment first.

examples.trans: They will grab it ahead of me.
I do not need to take the subway.

meanings.note: Opposite of bem; pegar mal means to look bad.

examples.trans: This is going to look really bad.

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: In Brazilian politics, ser cassado(a) means having one's electoral mandate revoked by the legislature or courts.

examples.trans: You have to get stripped of office.

meanings.note: Often reinforced with é que in questions (como é que foi?).

examples.text: Como é que foi a cirurgia?
Como é que tá meu marido?

meanings.note: Irregular past eu fiz (I made/did); não tem o que fazer means having nothing to do.

examples.text: Ela não tem o que fazer agora.
examples.trans: She has nothing to do now.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

meanings.note: Covers speaking, talking, and telling in everyday Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?

meanings.note: Very frequent general noun; singular muita coisa naturally translates as a lot of things.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

meanings.note: Modifies a verb to mean well or carefully, as in olhar bem (look closely).

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine singular.
In colloquial Brazilian speech, é tipo means 'it is kind of like'.

examples.text: É tipo um lençol de elástico.
examples.trans: It is like a fitted sheet.

examples.text: Que tipo de música você ouve?
examples.trans: What kind of music do you listen to?

meanings.note: Traditional everyday term for an Indigenous person in Brazil.

examples.text: Eles falaram sobre os índios do Brasil.
examples.trans: They spoke about the Indigenous peoples of Brazil.

examples.text: A história do índio está no livro.
examples.trans: The story of the Indigenous person is in the book.

meanings.note: Neutral pronoun for 'everything / all of it'.

examples.text: Vai ficar tudo bem com ele.
examples.trans: Everything is going to be fine with him.

meanings.note: Used either as a noun or predicate label; final -l is pronounced [w].

examples.text: O filme é sobre um canibal.
examples.trans: The movie is about a cannibal.

examples.text: Aquela história de canibal é antiga.

meanings.note: Used for machines, systems, and body organs.
Takes the preposition em (confiar em).

examples.text: Eu não confio em mapeamento eletrônico.
examples.trans: I do not trust electronic mapping.

examples.text: Você pode confiar na nossa equipe.

meanings.note: Everyday friendly farewell across Brazil, borrowed long ago from Italian ciao.
